doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Sampling and the estate's rights
summary: Whether the estate earns from samples of Skull Sessions, depends on who owns the music, and a pianist's album of his father's tunes without clearance.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: I noticed, I came across a thing I had not been aware of, of a 1975 recording called “Skull Music.”
“Skull Sessions.” And I noticed it said that some people have been sampling from that. Now does the estate get compensation for that?
They do if we own it. That’s the issue. To make sure that we own what they’re sampling see. Because if they sample with Universal stuff then we’ll get some but we’ll get half of

what Universal gets. But if it’s directly with me, and nobody’s contacted me yet and it’s interesting how people don’t contact you so much. I had this situation happen to me recently, and I want to be — this is a great pianist. He did an album with a lot of Dad’s tunes on it. So he contacted me because I work with ejazzline and he wanted to get permission to put his arrangements out. And they paid me a little bit for it so it works out real well. Well I never got clearance from the record company for the tunes originally. And it’s amazing, and everything has gone dead since then, just radio silence. You haven’t heard anything from anybody. And this guy told me, he said, “Well you know I thought the record company,” he told me who the guy was and I thought the record company was supposed to do that, and they were supposed to do that, but my issue is do I start to do copyright infringement because really the only people that really make money in that is the attorneys.
Yeah, you just might give yourself more headaches.
